{'test_behavior': 'Tests that lastIndexOfIgnoreCase returns the startPos when the searchStr is an empty CharSequence, covering the specific slice where empty search string handling occurs.\n', 'test_name': 'testLastIndexOfIgnoreCaseWithEmptySearchStringReturnsStartPos\n', 'test_code': '@Test\npublic void testLastIndexOfIgnoreCaseWithEmptySearchStringReturnsStartPos() {\n    // Test case 1: Empty search string with valid startPos in the middle\n    String str = "abcdef";\n    CharSequence searchStr = "";\n    int startPos = 3;\n    int result = StringUtils.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(str, searchStr, startPos);\n    assertEquals(3, result);\n\n    // Test case 2: Empty search string with startPos at the end\n    startPos = 6;\n    result = StringUtils.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(str, searchStr, startPos);\n    assertEquals(6, result);\n\n    // Test case 3: Empty search string with startPos at the beginning\n    startPos = 0;\n    result = StringUtils.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(str, searchStr, startPos);\n    assertEquals(0, result);\n\n    // Test case 4: Empty search string with startPos adjusted due to length constraints\n    // If startPos > str.length() - searchStr.length(), it gets adjusted.\n    // Since searchStr is empty, length is 0, so startPos remains as is unless negative.\n    startPos = 10; // Greater than string length\n    result = StringUtils.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(str, searchStr, startPos);\n    // The method adjusts startPos to str.length() - searchStr.length() = 6 - 0 = 6\n    // Then returns 6 because searchStr is empty.\n    assertEquals(6, result);\n}\n', 'new_imports_code': 'import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;\nimport org.junit.Test;'}

{'test_behavior': 'Tests that lastIndexOfIgnoreCase correctly finds the last occurrence of a search string in a case-insensitive manner when iterating backwards from a valid start position.', 'test_name': 'testLastIndexOfIgnoreCaseBackwardIterationCaseInsensitiveMatch', 'test_code': '@Test\npublic void testLastIndexOfIgnoreCaseBackwardIterationCaseInsensitiveMatch() {\n    // Test case: Search for "world" in "Hello World" starting from the end\n    // Expected: Should find "World" at index 6 despite case difference\n    String str = "Hello World";\n    String searchStr = "world";\n    int startPos = str.length() - 1; // Start from the last character\n    \n    int result = StringUtils.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(str, searchStr, startPos);\n    \n    assertEquals(6, result, "Should find \'world\' (case-insensitive) at index 6");\n    \n    // Additional test: Multiple occurrences, should return the last one before startPos\n    String str2 = "ABCabcABC";\n    String searchStr2 = "abc";\n    int startPos2 = str2.length() - 1;\n    \n    int result2 = StringUtils.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(str2, searchStr2, startPos2);\n    \n    assertEquals(6, result2, "Should find the last occurrence of \'abc\' at index 6");\n    \n    // Test with startPos limiting the search range\n    int startPos3 = 5; // Limit search to first half\n    int result3 = StringUtils.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(str2, searchStr2, startPos3);\n    \n    assertEquals(0, result3, "Should find the first occurrence of \'abc\' at index 0 when startPos is 5");\n}', 'new_imports_code': 'import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;\nimport org.junit.Test;'}

{'test_behavior': 'Verifies that the StringBuilder is initialized with an estimated capacity based on the number of items (noOfItems * 16) when joining a subset of the array, ensuring the logic path for buffer initialization is covered.\n', 'test_name': 'testStringBuilderCapacityInitialization\n', 'test_code': '@Test\npublic void testStringBuilderCapacityInitialization() {\n    // Arrange: Create an array with 3 elements to join from index 0 to 3 (noOfItems = 3)\n    // Expected capacity calculation: 3 * 16 = 48\n    Object[] array = new Object[] { "a", "b", "c" };\n    char separator = \',\';\n    int startIndex = 0;\n    int endIndex = 3;\n\n    // Act: Call the method under test\n    String result = StringUtils.join(array, separator, startIndex, endIndex);\n\n    // Assert: Verify the result is correct, which implies the StringBuilder was used correctly\n    // The specific internal capacity cannot be directly asserted without reflection or a custom mock,\n    // but exercising the code path with valid inputs ensures the initialization line is executed.\n    assertEquals("a,b,c", result);\n\n    // Additional case: Single item (noOfItems = 1), capacity = 16\n    Object[] singleArray = new Object[] { "x" };\n    String singleResult = StringUtils.join(singleArray, separator, 0, 1);\n    assertEquals("x", singleResult);\n\n    // Additional case: Multiple items to ensure loop and separator logic also run alongside initialization\n    Object[] multiArray = new Object[] { "one", "two", "three", "four" };\n    String multiResult = StringUtils.join(multiArray, \';\', 1, 4); // joins "two", "three", "four"\n    assertEquals("two;three;four", multiResult);\n}\n', 'new_imports_code': 'import org.junit.Test;\nimport static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;'}

{'test_behavior': 'Tests the loop logic where elements are joined with a separator, ensuring the separator is not added before the first element in the range, and null elements are skipped (treated as empty) while maintaining separator positions.\n', 'test_name': 'testJoinLoopWithSeparatorAndNulls\n', 'test_code': '@Test\npublic void testJoinLoopWithSeparatorAndNulls() {\n    Object[] array = {"A", null, "B", "C", null};\n    // Join from index 0 to 5 (full array)\n    String result = StringUtils.join(array, \';\', 0, 5);\n    assertEquals("A;;B;C;", result); \n    // Explanation: \n    // i=0: "A"\n    // i=1: null -> append separator then nothing -> "A;"\n    // i=2: "B" -> append separator then "B" -> "A;;B"\n    // i=3: "C" -> append separator then "C" -> "A;;B;C"\n    // i=4: null -> append separator then nothing -> "A;;B;C;"\n    \n    // Join from index 1 to 4 (null, "B", "C")\n    String result2 = StringUtils.join(array, \';\', 1, 4);\n    assertEquals(";B;C", result2);\n    // Explanation:\n    // i=1: null (first in range) -> ""\n    // i=2: "B" -> append separator then "B" -> ";B"\n    // i=3: "C" -> append separator then "C" -> ";B;C"\n    \n    // Join from index 2 to 3 (just "B")\n    String result3 = StringUtils.join(array, \';\', 2, 3);\n    assertEquals("B", result3);\n}\n', 'new_imports_code': 'import org.junit.Test;\nimport static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;'}

{'test_behavior': "Verifies that the StringBuilder is initialized with a capacity proportional to the number of items (noOfItems * 16) when joining a subarray of longs.\nThis test targets the specific slice where `final StringBuilder buf = new StringBuilder(noOfItems * 16);` is executed.\nIt uses an array of 5 elements, joining from index 1 to 4 (3 items), expecting an initial capacity of 48 (3 * 16).\nSince we cannot directly inspect the StringBuilder's capacity after the method returns the String,\nthis test validates the logical outcome of the join operation which relies on this buffer,\nand implicitly confirms the path execution. To strictly verify capacity logic without reflection in a black-box test,\nwe ensure the method completes successfully for a case where capacity estimation matters (non-empty, valid range).\nThe test asserts the correct joined string is produced, confirming the loop and buffer usage worked as intended.\n", 'test_name': 'testJoinLongArrayWithSubRangeInitialCapacity\n', 'test_code': '@Test\npublic void testJoinLongArrayWithSubRangeInitialCapacity() {\n    long[] array = {10L, 20L, 30L, 40L, 50L};\n    char separator = \',\';\n    int startIndex = 1;\n    int endIndex = 4;\n    \n    // Expected result: "20,30,40"\n    // Number of items = 4 - 1 = 3. Estimated capacity = 3 * 16 = 48.\n    String result = StringUtils.join(array, separator, startIndex, endIndex);\n    \n    assertEquals("20,30,40", result);\n}\n', 'new_imports_code': 'import org.junit.Test;\nimport static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;'}
